first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and simplifying onboarding has prior evidence of improving time-to-value and adoption. Verify that result alongside activation-messaging evidence, then run a controlled onboarding simplification test focused on qualified activation rather than reacting to competitor pricing with potentially lower-quality demand.

mid.rationale: Run a controlled simplification of onboarding because completion is down 4% and the verified result shows a substantial completion and time-to-value improvement, plus a durable 3% lift in 30-day retention. Measure qualified activation, time-to-value, and 30-day retention—not completion alone—to avoid trading shallow completion gains for lower-quality users. Activation messaging is also effective, but simplifying onboarding addresses both the immediate completion decline and the activation funnel earlier, with stronger retention evidence.

final2.rationale: The deeper competitor cut and doubled price-sensitive SMB churn make targeted promotional pricing the most direct response. Test it narrowly with eligible, price-sensitive SMB prospects or at-risk accounts, while guarding discount depth, gross margin, qualified revenue, retention, and post-promotion churn. The inherited evidence supports acquisition and revenue lift, but is not archive-verified this cycle, so avoid a broad rollout.
